# Load packages
```{r, warning = F, message = F}
library(tidyverse)
library(pammtools)
library(splines2)
library(posterior)
library(ggplot2)
library(rethinking)
library(survminer)
library(survival)
library(cowplot)
library(rstanarm)
library(bayestestR)
library(brms)
library(tidybayes)
library(bayesplot)
```





# I. Type
Coded as...
•	A
•	B
•	Intermediate


## 1. Previous studies for stenosis type


Locatelli et al., JSAP 2013
•	Valve morphology type B (thickened, hypoplastic annulus) → In whole population HR 3.33 (95%-CI 1·689-6·579)
  Intermediate type.  No difference cf type A, though exact figures not reported.
172 dogs


Chetboul et al. 2018
Did not assess type


Bonvin (Utrecht Thesis, 2019)
•	Valve morphology type B: poor outcome in PBV group (HR 7.026; 95%-CI 1.268-38.928)
  Intermediate type.  No difference cf type A, though exact figures not reported.
112 dogs



Use Bayes theorum to combine the evidence from these two studies to inform the prior for the effect of type B and AB on survival in our model
Use brm with estimate | se(error) to combine the evidence from the two studies, which allows us to use the point estimate and standard error (derived from the confidence intervals) from each study

SD (=sem) = (upperCI - lowerCI) / 3.92



## 1. Determine location and scale (sem) for type B
### a. Using Locatelli
```{r}
median_exp_l_type <- log(3.33)
lower_exp_l_type <- log(1.689)
upper_exp_l_type <- log(6.579)
range_l_type <- upper_exp_l_type - lower_exp_l_type
scale_l_type <- range_l_type / 3.96
prior_exp_l_type <- matrix(c(median_exp_l_type,
                    range_l_type,
                    scale_l_type)
)
colnames(prior_exp_l_type) <- "locatelli"
rownames(prior_exp_l_type) <- c("location", "range", "scale")
prior_exp_l_type
```



### b. Using Chetboul
```{r}
median_exp_c_type <- NA
lower_exp_c_type <- NA
upper_exp_c_type <- NA
range_c_type <- upper_exp_c_type - lower_exp_c_type
scale_c_type <- range_c_type / 4
prior_exp_c_type <- matrix(c(median_exp_c_type,
                    range_c_type,
                    scale_c_type)
)
colnames(prior_exp_c_type) <- "chetboul"
rownames(prior_exp_c_type) <- c("location", "range", "scale")
prior_exp_c_type
```




### c. Using Bonvin
```{r}
median_exp_b_type <- log(7.026)
lower_exp_b_type <- log(1.268)
upper_exp_b_type <- log(38.928)
range_b_type <- upper_exp_b_type - lower_exp_b_type
scale_b_type <- range_b_type / 3.96
prior_exp_b_type <- matrix(c(median_exp_b_type,
                    range_b_type,
                    scale_b_type)
)
colnames(prior_exp_b_type) <- "bonvin"
rownames(prior_exp_b_type) <- c("location", "range", "scale")
prior_exp_b_type
```





## 2. Set very weak neutral regularising prior 
very small datasets (1-3 values) , so prior could impact on the posterior significantly.  Therefore, set scale to 10, make prior virtually flat but not uniform.
```{r}
prior_type <- set_prior("normal(0, 10)", class = "b", coef = "Intercept")
```



## 3. Create a dataframe for the likelihood based on the Locatelli and Bonvin studies
```{r}
df_type <- data.frame(
  estimate = c(median_exp_l_type, median_exp_c_type, median_exp_b_type), # Observed scale for all studies
  error = c(scale_l_type, scale_c_type, scale_b_type)      # Observed SD (Standard Error) for all studies
)
```



## 4. Run model
```{r}
set.seed(999)
model_type <- brm(estimate | se(error) ~ 0 + Intercept,
                   family = gaussian(),
                   data = df_type,
                   prior = prior_type,
                   control=list(adapt_delta=0.98),
                   iter = 2000, warmup = 1000,
                   save_pars = save_pars(all =TRUE),
                   sample_prior = TRUE)
```



## View MCMC trace plots
```{r}
color_scheme_set("mix-blue-pink")
posterior_model_type <- as.array(model_type)
mcmc_trace(posterior_model_type)
```



### b. Trace rank plot
```{r}
color_scheme_set("viridis")
mcmc_rank_overlay(posterior_model_type) +
  ylim(0, 100)
```




## 5. get summary of model
```{r}
summary(model_type)
```

## 6. Get location (median estimate) and scale (SD)
```{r}
draws <- as.matrix(model_type)
location_type <- mean(draws[,1]) # draws for type_b
scale_type <- sd(draws[,1])
location_type
scale_type
```



## 7. Compare prior and posterior
```{r}
plot(hypothesis(model_type, "Intercept = 0"))
```




## 8. Decision...
Set an informative prior...
 ~ student_t(df = 3, location = 1.292032, scale = 0.3219278)


### a. Prior for beta of type
```{r}
prior_beta_type <- student_t(df = 3, location = location_type, scale = scale_type, autoscale = FALSE)
```



### b. Suggested scales assuming strong, moderate and weak priors.
Given such a small scale, best to adjust the strong prior is based on the combined estimate from the literature, whilst moderate and weak priors are then scaled up from the strong prior.  These latter priors ensure that the data are not overwhelmed by the prior, but still allow for some regularisation to improve model convergence and reduce overfitting.
Therefore, strong prior should be 1x the combine scale, then increase this by 2x for moderate and 4x for weak.
```{r}
strong_scale <- scale_type
moderate_scale <- strong_scale * 2
weak_scale <- strong_scale * 4

prior_scale_type <- matrix(c(strong_scale,
                        moderate_scale,
                        weak_scale)
)
colnames(prior_scale_type) <- "suggested scale"
rownames(prior_scale_type) <- c("strong", "moderate", "weak")
prior_scale_type
```



### c. Priors bin
```{r}
priors_bin_type <- list(
  weak = student_t(df = 3, location = location_type, scale = weak_scale, autoscale = TRUE),
  moderate = student_t(df = 3, location = location_type, scale = moderate_scale, autoscale = TRUE),
  strong = student_t(df = 3, location = location_type, scale = strong_scale, autoscale = TRUE)
)
```





## 9. Plot comparison of study distribution vs. posterior
### a. Generate posterior for plotting
```{r}
# 1. Extract the Posterior and Prior draws
draws <- model_type %>%
  spread_draws(b_Intercept) %>%
  dplyr::rename(Posterior = b_Intercept) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = Posterior, names_to = "Source", values_to = "Value")

# 2. Define the Likelihood parameters (from Locatelli study)
locatelli_med <- median_exp_l_type
locatelli_se   <- scale_l_type 

# 3. Define the Likelihood parameters (from Chetboul study)
chetboul_med <- median_exp_c_type
chetboul_se   <- scale_c_type 

# 4. Define the Likelihood parameters (from Bonvin study)
bonvin_med <- median_exp_b_type
bonvin_se   <- scale_b_type 
```



### b. Create the density plot
```{r}
# Create the Plot
ggplot() +
  # LAYER 1: Posterior (from your HMC draws)
  geom_density(
    data = draws, 
    aes(x = Value), 
    alpha = 0.7,
    color = "black",
    linewidth = 1
  ) +

  
  # LAYER 2: Distribution from Locatelli (Generated mathematically to match the others)
  # We use stat_function with 'geom = "area"' to create a shaded shape
  stat_function(
    data = data.frame(Value = c(locatelli_med - 3.92 * locatelli_se, locatelli_med + 3.92 * locatelli_se)), 
    aes(x = Value, fill = "Locatelli"),
    fun = dnorm, 
    args = list(mean = locatelli_med , sd = locatelli_se),
    geom = "area",
    alpha = 0.2,
    inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +

   # LAYER 3: Distribution from Chetboul (Generated mathematically to match the others)
  # We use stat_function with 'geom = "area"' to create a shaded shape
  stat_function(
    data = data.frame(Value = c(chetboul_med - 3.92 * chetboul_se, chetboul_med + 3.92 * chetboul_se)), 
    aes(x = Value, fill = "Chetboul"),
    fun = dnorm, 
    args = list(mean = chetboul_med, sd = chetboul_se),
    geom = "area",
    alpha = 0.2,
    inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) + 

    # LAYER 4: Distribution from Bonvin (Generated mathematically to match the others)
  # We use stat_function with 'geom = "area"' to create a shaded shape
  stat_function(
    data = data.frame(Value = c(bonvin_med - 3.92 * bonvin_se, bonvin_med + 3.92 * bonvin_se)), 
    aes(x = Value, fill = "Bonvin"),
    fun = dnorm, 
    args = list(mean = bonvin_med, sd = bonvin_se),
    geom = "area",
    alpha = 0.2,
    inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +  
  
    
  # Styling the Colors
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Locatelli" = "#F8766D",
      "Chetboul" = "#619CFF",
      "Bonvin" = "#00BA38"
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Informed prior for effect of type B on survival",
    subtitle = "Visualising how the Posterior reconciles Locatelli and Bonvin",
    x = "Effect Estimate",
    y = "Density",
    fill = "Component"
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = c(0.9, 0.8)) +
  labs(fill = "Study") +

           theme(axis.title.y = element_text(size=12, face="bold"), 
               axis.title.x = element_text(size=12, face="bold"),
               plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size=14, face="bold"),
               plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12, hjust = 0.5, face = "italic"),
               axis.text.x = element_text(color = "grey50", size = 10),
               axis.text.y = element_text(color = "grey50",size = 10)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype="dotted", 
                color = "firebrick", linewidth = 1.5)
```












# II. Age (in months)
Coded as...
•	Standardised
•	SD = 19.4778645
•	mean 18 months, median 11 months, range 2 to 132 months


## Previous studies for age

Chetboul et al
•	Age (years) — HR = 2.3 per 1-year increase, p = 0.02... 
•	(Older age at diagnosis associated with shorter time to cardiac death).
2.3 (per 1 year increase; 95% CI¼ 1.2-4.4; p= 0.02)


Scansen
•	Younger age at diagnosis (discussed as suggesting more severe disease in some contexts) — presented as a factor clinicians consider for earlier intervention (not shown as a quantified HR in the review).

Locatelli et al., JSAP 2013
•	Younger age at diagnosis (<1 year) → poorer survival.
dogs <1y HR 3·96 (1·837-8·307)
No average age stated, so assume this is ~2 SD away from the mean
That way age effect per year would be...
### Invert HRs to get change per SD age
```{r}
# mean
1/3.96

# lower 95%-CI
1/8.307

# upper 95%-CI
1/1.837
```

Bonvin
Found a linear increase in HR per month of age as 1.020 (1.001-1.039)




## Determine coefficient for age
### a. Using Locatelli
NB Assume <12 months is a 1 SD change from location
```{r}
median_exp_l_age <- log(0.2525253)
lower_exp_l_age <- log(0.1203804)
upper_exp_l_age <- log(0.5443658)
range_l_age <- upper_exp_l_age - lower_exp_l_age
scale_l_age <- range_l_age / 3.96
prior_exp_l_age <- matrix(c(median_exp_l_age,
                    range_l_age,
                    scale_l_age)
)
colnames(prior_exp_l_age) <- "locatelli"
rownames(prior_exp_l_age) <- c("location", "range", "scale")
prior_exp_l_age
```





### b. Using Chetboul
```{r}
median_exp_c_age <- log(2.3 ^ (19/12))
lower_exp_c_age <- log(1.2 ^ (19/12))
upper_exp_c_age <- log(4.4 ^ (19/12))
range_c_age <- upper_exp_c_age - lower_exp_c_age
scale_c_age <- range_c_age / 3.96
prior_exp_c_age <- matrix(c(median_exp_c_age,
                    range_c_age,
                    scale_c_age)
)
colnames(prior_exp_c_age) <- "chetboul"
rownames(prior_exp_c_age) <- c("location", "range", "scale")
prior_exp_c_age
```



### c. Using Bonvin
HRs presented per month of age
Need to standardise to 1 SD of current study which is 19 months
Therefore, multiply by 19
```{r}
median_exp_b_age <- log(1.020 ^ 19)
lower_exp_b_age <- log(1.001 ^ 19)
upper_exp_b_age <- log(1.039 ^ 19)
range_b_age <- upper_exp_b_age - lower_exp_b_age
scale_b_age <- range_b_age / 3.96 
prior_exp_b_age <- matrix(c(median_exp_b_age,
                    range_b_age,
                    scale_b_age)
)
colnames(prior_exp_b_age) <- "bonvin"
rownames(prior_exp_b_age) <- c("location", "range", "scale")
prior_exp_b_age
```

# III. Surgery
Coded as...
•	0 (no)
•	1 (yes)


## 1, Previous studies for surgery

Locatelli et al., JSAP 2013
•	Treatment effect: PBV improved survival in severe PS; asymptomatic moderate PS also had better outcomes.
balloon valvuloplasty (HR 0·47, P=0·047) 
no BVP in severe PS (HR 2·11, 95%CI 1·011-4·396) 
Inverse are HRs for BVP (nb severe PS)...
```{r}
1/2.11
1/1.011
1/4.396
```
Therefore, HR of 0.47 for use of bv in severe PS, and HR of 0.23 to 0.99 for use of bv in moderate PS.




Bonvin (Utrecht Thesis, 2019)
•	PBV treatment: protective factor, significantly prolongs survival in severe PS
Severe and moderate BBP... HR 0.339 (0.135-0.854)

## 8. Decision...
Set an informative prior...
 ~ student_t(df = 3, location = -0.879165, scale = 0.2911939)



### a. Prior for beta of surgery
```{r}
prior_beta_sx <- student_t(df = 3, location = location_sx, scale = scale_sx, autoscale = TRUE)
```




### b. Suggested scales assuming strong, moderate and weak priors.
Given such a small scale, best to adjustThe strong prior is based on the combined estimate from the literature, whilst moderate and weak priors are then scaled up from the strong prior.  These latter priors ensure that the data are not overwhelmed by the prior, but still allow for some regularisation to improve model convergence and reduce overfitting.
Therefore, strong prior should be 1x the combine scale, then increase this by 2.5x for moderate and 5x for weak.
```{r}
strong_scale <- scale_sx
moderate_scale <- strong_scale * 2
weak_scale <- strong_scale * 4

prior_scale_sx <- matrix(c(strong_scale,
                        moderate_scale,
                        weak_scale)
)
colnames(prior_scale_sx) <- "suggested scale"
rownames(prior_scale_sx) <- c("strong", "moderate", "weak")
prior_scale_sx
```



### c. Priors bin
```{r}
priors_bin_sx <- list(
  weak = student_t(df = 3, location = location_sx, scale = weak_scale, autoscale = TRUE),
  moderate = student_t(df = 3, location = location_sx, scale = moderate_scale, autoscale = TRUE),
  strong = student_t(df = 3, location = location_sx, scale = strong_scale, autoscale = TRUE)
)
```

### a. Generate posterior for plotting
```{r}

draws <- model_sx %>%
  spread_draws(b_Intercept) %>%
  dplyr::rename(Posterior = b_Intercept) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = Posterior, names_to = "Source", values_to = "Value")

# 2. Define the Likelihood parameters (from Locatelli study)

locatelli_se   <- scale_l_sx

# 3. Define the Likelihood parameters (from Chetboul study)

chetboul_se   <- scale_c_sx

# 4. Define the Likelihood parameters (from Bonvin study)

bonvin_se   <- scale_b_sx
```



### b. Create the density plot
```{r}
# Create the Plot
ggplot() +
  # LAYER 1: Posterior (from your HMC draws)
  geom_density(
    data = draws, 
    aes(x = Value), 
    alpha = 0.7,
    color = "black",
    linewidth = 1
  ) +

  
  # LAYER 2: Distribution from Locatelli (Generated mathematically to match the others)
  # We use stat_function with 'geom = "area"' to create a shaded shape
  stat_function(
    data = data.frame(Value = c(locatelli_med - 3.96*locatelli_se, locatelli_med + 3.96*locatelli_se)), 
    aes(x = Value, fill = "Locatelli"),
    fun = dnorm, 
    args = list(mean = locatelli_med , sd = locatelli_se),
    geom = "area",
    alpha = 0.2,
    inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +

   # LAYER 3: Distribution from Chetboul (Generated mathematically to match the others)
  # We use stat_function with 'geom = "area"' to create a shaded shape
  stat_function(
    data = data.frame(Value = c(chetboul_med - 3.96 * chetboul_se, chetboul_med + 3.96 * chetboul_se)), 
    aes(x = Value, fill = "Chetboul"),
    fun = dnorm, 
    args = list(mean = chetboul_med, sd = chetboul_se),
    geom = "area",
    alpha = 0.2,
    inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) + 

    # LAYER 4: Distribution from Bonvin (Generated mathematically to match the others)
  # We use stat_function with 'geom = "area"' to create a shaded shape
  stat_function(
    data = data.frame(Value = c(bonvin_med - 3.96 * bonvin_se, bonvin_med + 3.96 * bonvin_se)), 
    aes(x = Value, fill = "Bonvin"),
    fun = dnorm, 
    args = list(mean = bonvin_med, sd = bonvin_se),
    geom = "area",
    alpha = 0.2,
    inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +  
  
    
  # Styling the Colors
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Locatelli" = "#F8766D",
      "Chetboul" = "#619CFF",
      "Bonvin" = "#00BA38"
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Informed prior for effect of intervention on survival",
    subtitle = "Visualising how the Posterior reconciles Locatell and Bonvin",
    x = "Effect Estimate",
    y = "Density",
    fill = "Component"
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = c(0.9, 0.8)) +
  labs(fill = "Study") +

           theme(axis.title.y = element_text(size=12, face="bold"), 
               axis.title.x = element_text(size=12, face="bold"),
               plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size=14, face="bold"),
               plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12, hjust = 0.5, face = "italic"),
               axis.text.x = element_text(color = "grey50", size = 10),
               axis.text.y = element_text(color = "grey50",size = 10)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype="dotted", 
                color = "firebrick", linewidth = 1.5)
```

# V. PRESSURE GRADIENT (pv_max_pg)
Coded as...
•	Standardised
•	SD = 40.9438358


## 1. Previous studies about pressure gradient


Scansen, Advances in the Treatment of Pulmonary Valve Stenosis
•	High transpulmonary pressure gradient higher gradients linked to worse prognosis and are used to justify intervention.



### a. Using Locatelli
•	Pulmonary Doppler gradient in dogs not having balloon valvuloplasty: higher DG = worse survival
Moderate PS... HR 1·02 (95%-CI 1·009-1·032) per mmHg increase in pressure gradient

1SD in the current study is 40.9438358 mmHg, so HR per 1 SD increase in pressure gradient would be..
```{r}
median_exp_l_pv <- log(1.02 ^ 40.9438358)
lower_exp_l_pv <- log(1.009 ^ 40.9438358)
upper_exp_l_pv <- log(1.032 ^ 40.9438358)
range_l_pv <- upper_exp_l_pv - lower_exp_l_pv
scale_l_pv <- range_l_pv / 3.92
prior_exp_l_pv <- matrix(c(median_exp_l_pv,
                    range_l_pv,
                    scale_l_pv)
)
colnames(prior_exp_l_pv) <- "locatelli"
rownames(prior_exp_l_pv) <- c("location", "range", "scale")
prior_exp_l_pv
```



### b. Using Chetboul 2018
Journal of Veterinary Cardiology (2018) 20, 405e414

•	Pulmonary Doppler gradient: higher DG = worse survival
HR 1.2 (95%-CI 1.0-1.3) per 10 mmHg increase in pressure gradient
NB per 10 mmHg so multiply by 4.09438358 and NOT 40.9438358
```{r}
median_exp_c_pv <- log(1.2 ^ 4.09438358)
lower_exp_c_pv <- log(1.0 ^ 4.09438358)
upper_exp_c_pv <- log(1.3 ^ 4.09438358)
range_c_pv <- upper_exp_c_pv - lower_exp_c_pv
scale_c_pv <- range_c_pv / 3.92
prior_exp_c_pv <- matrix(c(median_exp_c_pv,
                    range_c_pv,
                    scale_c_pv)
)
colnames(prior_exp_c_pv) <- "chetboul"
rownames(prior_exp_c_pv) <- c("location", "range", "scale")
prior_exp_c_pv
```



### c. Using Bonvin (Utrecht Thesis, 2019)
•	Pulmonary Doppler gradient: higher DG = worse survival
Moderate PS... HR 1.012 (95%-CI 1.001-1.023) per mmHg increase in pressure gradient
Severe PS... HR 1.013 (95%-CI 1.001-1.026) per mmHg increase in pressure gradient

1SD in the current study is 40.9438358 mmHg, so HR per 1 SD increase in pressure gradient would be..
```{r}
median_exp_b_pv <- log(1.0125 ^ 40.9438358)
lower_exp_b_pv <- log(1.001 ^ 40.9438358)
upper_exp_b_pv <- log(1.0245 ^ 40.9438358)
range_b_pv <- upper_exp_b_pv - lower_exp_b_pv
scale_b_pv <- range_b_pv / 3.92
prior_exp_b_pv <- matrix(c(median_exp_b_pv,
                    range_b_pv,
                    scale_b_pv)
)
colnames(prior_exp_b_pv) <- "bonvin"
rownames(prior_exp_b_pv) <- c("location", "range", "scale")
prior_exp_b_pv
```



## 2. Set very weak neutral regularising prior 
very small datasets (1-3 values) , so prior could impact on the posterior significantly.  Therefore, set scale to 10, make prior virtually flat but not uniform.
```{r}
prior_pv <- set_prior("normal(0, 10)", class = "b", coef = "Intercept")
```




## 3. Create a dataframe for the likelihood based on the Chetboul study
```{r}
df_pv <- data.frame(
  estimate = c(median_exp_l_pv, median_exp_c_pv, median_exp_b_pv), # Observed scales for all studies
  error = c(scale_l_pv, scale_c_pv, scale_b_pv)      # Observed SD (Standard Error) for all studies
)
```





## 4. Run model
```{r}
set.seed(999)
model_pv <- brm(estimate | se(error) ~ 0 + Intercept,
                   family = gaussian(),
                   data = df_pv,
                   prior = prior_pv,
                   control=list(adapt_delta=0.98),
                   iter = 2000, warmup = 1000,
                   save_pars = save_pars(all =TRUE),
                   sample_prior = TRUE)
```



## View MCMC trace plots
```{r}
color_scheme_set("mix-blue-pink")
posterior_model_pv <- as.array(model_pv)
mcmc_trace(posterior_model_pv)
```



### b. Trace rank plot
```{r}
color_scheme_set("viridis")
mcmc_rank_overlay(posterior_model_pv) +
  ylim(0, 100)
```




## 5. get summary of model
```{r}
summary(model_pv)
```

```{r}
location_pv <- mean(draws[,1]) # draws for type
scale_pv <- sd(draws[,1])
location_pv
scale_pv
```

### c.Bonvin (Utrecht Thesis, 2019)
•	Atenolol therapy: paradoxically associated with shorter survival in PBV dogs
6.349 (1.198-33.641)
```{r}
median_exp_b_atenolol <- log(6.349)
lower_exp_b_atenolol<- log(1.198)
upper_exp_b_atenolol <- log(33.641)
range_b_atenolol <- upper_exp_b_atenolol - lower_exp_b_atenolol
scale_b_atenolol <- range_b_atenolol / 4

prior_exp_b_atenolol
```





## 2. Set very weak neutral regularising prior 
very small datasets (1-3 values) , so prior could impact on the posterior significantly.  Therefore, set scale to 10, make prior virtually flat but not uniform.
```{r}
prior_atenolol <- set_prior("normal(0, 10)", class = "b", coef = "Intercept")
```




## 3. Create a dataframe for the likelihood based on the Chetboul study
```{r}
df_atenolol <- data.frame(
  estimate = c(median_exp_l_atenolol, median_exp_c_atenolol, median_exp_b_atenolol), # Observed scales for all studies
  error = c(scale_l_atenolol, scale_c_atenolol, scale_b_atenolol)      # Observed SD (Standard Error) for all studies
)
```





## 4. Run model
```{r}
set.seed(999)
model_atenolol <- brm(estimate | se(error) ~ 0 + Intercept,
                   family = gaussian(),
                   data = df_atenolol,
                   prior = prior_atenolol,
                   control=list(adapt_delta=0.98),
                   iter = 2000, warmup = 1000,
                   save_pars = save_pars(all =TRUE),
                   sample_prior = TRUE)
```



## View MCMC trace plots




## 8. Decision...
Set an informative prior...
 ~ student_t(df = 3, location = 1.866284, scale = 0.8443848)


### a. Prior for beta of pv_max
```{r}
prior_beta_atenolol <- student_t(df = 3, location = location_atenolol, scale = scale_atenolol, autoscale = TRUE)
```




### b. Suggested scales assuming strong, moderate and weak priors.
The strong prior is based on the combined estimate from the literature, whilst moderate and weak priors are then scaled up from the strong prior.  These latter priors ensure that the data are not overwhelmed by the prior, but still allow for some regularisation to improve model convergence and reduce overfitting.
Therefore, strong prior should be 1x the combine scale, then increase this by 2x for moderate and 4x for weak.
```{r}
strong_scale <- scale_atenolol
moderate_scale <- strong_scale * 2
weak_scale <- strong_scale * 4

prior_scale_atenolol <- matrix(c(strong_scale,
                        moderate_scale,
                        weak_scale)
)
colnames(prior_scale_atenolol) <- "suggested scale"
rownames(prior_scale_atenolol) <- c("strong", "moderate", "weak")
prior_scale_atenolol
```



### c. Priors bin
```{r}
priors_bin_atenolol <- list(
  weak = student_t(df = 3, location = location_atenolol, scale = weak_scale, autoscale = TRUE),
  moderate = student_t(df = 3, location = location_atenolol, scale = moderate_scale, autoscale = TRUE),
  strong = student_t(df = 3, location = location_atenolol, scale = strong_scale, autoscale = TRUE)
)
```
